request.system: You design a structured interview blueprint. Given a job profile and a target number of main questions, produce exactly that many question slots that together give broad, non-overlapping coverage of the role's most important skills and focus areas. Order them to flow naturally — foundational topics before advanced ones. Calibrate each difficulty to the stated seniority. Each slot names the specific skill to test, the intent (what to assess), a difficulty, and the key points a strong answer should cover — the concepts, tradeoffs, and edge cases later used to grade the candidate's answer.

messages.content:
Job context:
- Company: Meridian Commerce
- Target role: Data Engineer, Streaming Platform
- Seniority: mid
- Key skills to assess: Kafka, Flink, Iceberg, S3, SQL, Python, stream processing, lakehouse, data contracts, exactly-once semantics, dbt, AWS
- Focus areas: event pipeline architecture, stream processing, data quality and contracts, cost optimization, analytics infrastructure, ML data pipelines

Design exactly 2 interview question slots for this role.

skill.description: The specific skill or topic this question tests, e.g. 'Kubernetes networking'.
skill.title: Skill

intent.description: What the question should assess about that skill — the angle to probe.
intent.title: Intent

difficulty.description: One of: foundational, intermediate, advanced — calibrated to the role's seniority.
difficulty.title: Difficulty

key_points.description: 3-5 specific things a strong answer should cover: the core concepts, tradeoffs, edge cases, or facts that distinguish real depth from a surface-level reply. Each a short phrase. Used later to grade answers, so be concrete and answer-focused, not a restatement of the question.
key_points.title: Key Points

slots.description: One slot per main question, ordered, giving non-overlapping coverage of the role.
slots.title: Slots

slots.intent: Assess ability to design and troubleshoot production event pipelines, including topic design, partitioning strategy, and handling of backpressure and failure modes
key_points: partition key selection and its impact on ordering and load distribution
consumer group semantics and lag management in streaming context
rebalancing behavior and its operational implications
handling poison pills and malformed messages without blocking the pipeline
trade-offs between throughput, latency, and resource consumption

slots.skill: Stream processing with Flink and exactly-once semantics
slots.intent: Evaluate understanding of stateful stream processing, checkpointing strategies, and guarantees needed for accurate lakehouse data ingestion and analytics
key_points: difference between at-least-once, exactly-once, and idempotence; when each is appropriate
checkpoint and savepoint mechanics and recovery guarantees
state backend choices (RocksDB vs in-memory) and their cost/performance trade-offs
windowing operations and late-arriving data handling
integration with Iceberg for exactly-once writes and atomicity

slots.skill: Data contracts and quality in streaming pipelines
slots.intent: Assess ability to define and enforce data quality standards, schema evolution, and alerting in continuous data flows to prevent downstream analytics failures
key_points: schema registry role and schema evolution strategies (backward, forward, full compatibility)
data quality metrics and assertions that catch issues early (nullability, range, cardinality, freshness)
alert thresholds and observability instrumentation for streaming jobs
handling breaking schema changes and versioning in multi-consumer environments
trade-off between strict validation (latency cost) and permissive ingestion (downstream cost)

slots.intent: Evaluate design decisions around Iceberg table format, partitioning, compaction, and S3 access patterns to balance query performance, operational complexity, and cloud costs
key_points: Iceberg hidden partitioning and partition evolution advantages over Hive-style partitioning
file sizing and compaction frequency impact on small-file problem and query latency
time-travel and schema evolution capabilities and their operational value
S3 request costs and optimization through intelligent partitioning and caching strategies
trade-offs between real-time ingestion frequency and batch compaction windows
